newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB - Ukraine could export 0.85 mln T sunseed.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Ukraine could export 0.85 mln T sunseed.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
UKRAINE COULD EXPORT 0.85 MILLION TONNES OF SUNFLOWER SEEDS IN 1996-1997
MOSCOW, Dec 20 - Ukraine will be able to export up to 0.85 million tonnes of sunseeds in 1996-1997 (October-September) despite a 19 percent fall in output in the 1996 crop on 1995.

This reflects the continued decline in domestic demand for sunflower oil, reduced sunflower oil deliveries to Russia because of increased competition with other suppliers, and the introduction of value added tax on Ukrainian goods delivered to Russia since September 1.

Sunseed exports contracted this autumn have been reported at 0.5 million tonnes of sunseeds, but due to low international prices, many contracts have been postponed to March-April 1997, when world prices are expected to increase.
As result of the reduced export demand, domestic wholesale prices declined 4-6 percent from September to November and currently sunseed domestic prices are 75-80 percent of world prices.
Ukraine's total sunseed production in 1996 is officially estimated at 2.3 million tonnes, 19 percent down on last year.
Average sunseed yields fell to 1.13 tonnes per hectare due to unfavorable weather conditions and shortages of hybrid seeds which resulted in losses of some 0.35-0.5 million tonnes in annual output.
Only 30 percent of sunseed acreage in 1996 was sown by hybrid seeds. Producers need at least 9,000-10,000 tonnes of hybrid seeds.
Sunseed production in Ukraine remains more profitable than grain and sugarbeet farming, although production costs increased in 1996 to $90.1 per tonne, against $44.7 per tonne last year.
Estimated sunseed profitability (revenue/cost ratio) in 1996 was at 175.0 percent, against 157.0 percent and 107.5 percent, respectively for grain and sugarbeet production.
Sunseed exports are the major source of hard currency earnings for Ukrainian farmers.
